title: Mapping General-Purpose AI Governance Across Twenty AI Middle-Power Jurisdictions
note: Primary source [1]. Working paper, not peer reviewed, data snapshot 2026-07-30. Source of every provision, instrument, actor and definition figure in this report.

title: Accompanying dataset for "Mapping General-Purpose AI Governance Across Twenty AI Middle-Power Jurisdictions"
note: Primary source [2]. CC BY 4.0. Tables of 101 instruments, 144 actors and 52 definitions, plus the out-of-scope instrument appendix. The 587 clause-level records are not included in this version.

title: Designing Escalation Criteria for International AI Incident Response
note: Adjacent literature [3]. Source of the detection asymmetry concept. Two authors overlap with the primary source and the first author co-designed its codebook, so this is the same team's earlier work rather than independent prior research.

title: Training Compute Thresholds: Features and Functions in AI Regulation
note: Adjacent literature [4]. Argues training compute is currently the best available first-pass filter for regulatory oversight. The claim that thresholds trigger nothing is not from this paper; it is the primary source's finding about its own sample.

title: The Global Majority in International AI Governance
note: Adjacent literature [5]. Source of the observation that sectoral routes trade permanence for speed and compliance pressure.

title: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 of 8 July 2026 (Digital Omnibus on AI)
container-title: Official Journal of the European Union
note: Law/policy [6]. Published 2026-07-24, in force 2026-07-27. Source for the AI Office's investigation, on-site inspection, binding commitment, fine and periodic penalty powers and the widened exclusive supervisory perimeter (text checked 2026-08-24).

title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (EU AI Act)
container-title: Official Journal of the European Union
note: Law/policy [7]. Article 52 (rebuttable presumption of systemic risk), Article 55(1)(a) and (c), Article 73.

title: 인공지능 발전과 신뢰 기반 조성 등에 관한 기본법 (Framework Act on the Development of Artificial Intelligence and Establishment of a Foundation of Trust)
note: Law/policy [8]. Enforcement Decree in force 2026-01-22, Article 24(1) — the three cumulative conditions of compute, state-of-the-art technology and serious risk.

title: AI 기본법 시행령 제정안 입법예고
note: Law/policy [9]. Grace period on administrative fines of at least one year and the integrated support centre. Confirmed via Electronic Times reporting of 2025-11-12 (article, in Korean).

title: 금융분야 AI 가이드라인 (Financial Sector AI Guidelines)
note: Law/policy [10]. The only Korean serious incident reporting provision coded by the paper.

title: PL 2338/2023
note: Law/policy [11]. Passed the Senate 2024-12-10, pending in a Chamber of Deputies special committee (checked 2026-08).

title: Artificial Intelligence Bill 2026 (Senate Bills No. 4)
note: Law/policy [12]. First Senate reading 2026-04-02, referred to the ICT standing committee, not enacted as of August 2026.

title: CNJ Resolução nº 615/2025 (governance of generative AI in the Brazilian judiciary)
note: Law/policy [13]. 72-hour reporting of harmful events, with corrective measures.

title: Towards a Common Reporting Framework for AI Incidents
note: Law/policy [14]. Proposes 29 criteria for what an incident report should contain.

title: AI Index Report 2026
container-title: Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence
note: Law/policy [15]. AI Incident Database tally of 362 incidents in 2025 and 233 in 2024, cited via the primary source.
